strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Moves the next post-provenance Mode Pack candidate-approval route boundary from caller-supplied typed-target assembly into Rust-owned replay-safe journey continuation.
Continues an admitted journey through existing headless.run.drive/headless.run.advance authority across a third explicit Mode Pack route boundary while preserving stop-boundary behavior.
Keeps approval route eligibility, target derivation, trusted-checkpoint binding, replay, and denial in the Rust runtime rather than the VSIX or headless caller.
Binds approval route resume to selected-candidate provenance-verification and fetch checkpoints so a headless caller can recover from bounded runtime state.
Returns bounded approval route-resume metadata with source checkpoint fingerprint, derived target class, result continuation, post-route progress, replay state, and next action.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with supporting agent_loop, mode_pack_runtime, runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, context_management, and progress_visualization.
answers.new_capability: headless.run.drive can accept one explicitly authorized journey_route_resume envelope and derive a selected-candidate approval target from persisted selected-candidate provenance-verification plus fetch checkpoint evidence without caller-supplied modepack_selected_candidate_approval_target.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M50.2 derives the selected-candidate fetch target and M50.3 derives the provenance-verification target, while M49.3 can approve a candidate only when the caller supplies the typed approval target. The next trusted approval route boundary still remained outside Rust-owned journey execution.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A scheduled caller would still need external glue to inspect provenance/fetch evidence, build trusted candidate-approval targets, and manage lost-response replay outside the Rust execution authority.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M50.3 provenance route resume, M50.2 fetch route resume, and M50.1 journey admission because it crosses the next post-provenance candidate-approval boundary.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing headless.run.drive method is extended with one additional bounded journey_route_resume route kind and result metadata.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase adds executable approval route continuation, checkpoint validation, ledger evidence, and replay behavior rather than a report, digest, readiness, history, or inspection surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The Rust runtime validates journey fingerprint, session sequence, route kind, selected-candidate provenance-verification checkpoint fingerprint, referenced fetch checkpoint consistency, approval authorization, trusted evidence identity, and replay identity; derives a ModePackSelectedCandidateApprovalTarget; executes it through existing continuation authority; persists bounded resume evidence; and replays without duplicate approval side effects.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A headless controller can continue a Golden Journey from provenance verification into candidate approval after a crash or boundary stop without reconstructing trusted approval target identity in the caller.
answers.milestone_progress: Adds the third runtime-derived post-admission Mode Pack route continuation needed before M50 can reach approved-candidate replacement, closure, and end-to-end Golden Journey completion.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M50.4 updates the current and archived phase-value manifests for a product runtime candidate-approval route-resume phase. Review must confirm the manifest change does not weaken phase-value, product-completion, diagnostics, or source-of-truth enforcement.

exit_criteria: headless.run.drive accepts one authorized bounded approval journey-route resume envelope without adding a new RPC

the runtime derives a selected-candidate approval target from persisted selected-candidate provenance-verification and fetch checkpoint evidence instead of requiring caller-supplied modepack_selected_candidate_approval_target

journey-route resume validates journey fingerprint, current session sequence, route kind, source provenance-verification checkpoint fingerprint, referenced fetch checkpoint consistency, authorization, trusted evidence identity, and replay identity before route side effects

unsupported route kind, missing authorization, stale checkpoint fingerprint, missing provenance checkpoint, missing fetch checkpoint, checkpoint-evidence mismatch, and mixed explicit target requests fail closed without new approval, drive, or resume evidence
replaying the same resume request returns committed bounded metadata without duplicating candidate approval, drive, or journey-route resume ledger evidence

resume result metadata contains bounded journey/task/run/session/drive handles, route kind, source checkpoint fingerprint, derived target class, result advance/continuation id, post-route progress, next action, replay flag, and deterministic resume fingerprint

VSIX validators accept fetch, provenance, and approval bounded route-resume protocol shapes and reject malformed fingerprints, false authorization, mixed explicit targets, mismatched derived target classes, and raw/unbounded fields
no report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, generic scheduler, new RPC, or VSIX-owned policy is added

Rust M50.1 journey admission tests continue covering journey admission denial, malformed journey ids, mixed admission targets, and conflicting replay boundaries

VSIX runtimeClient protocol tests accept valid fetch, provenance, and approval journey_route_resume params and journey_route_resume result metadata, reject mixed explicit targets, non-unit route budgets, malformed fingerprints, mismatched derived target class, and raw route-resume fields

safety_boundary: reuses existing headless.run.drive and headless.run.advance authority; no new JSON-RPC method is added
FetchSelectedModePackCandidateExplicitly, VerifySelectedModePackCandidateProvenanceExplicitly, and ApproveVerifiedModePackCandidateExplicitly are supported by route resume after M50.4
route resume cannot mix journey admission, caller-supplied explicit Mode Pack targets, context budgets, or completion finalization authorization
the source checkpoint fingerprint, referenced fetch/provenance checkpoint evidence, and current session sequence must match before route side effects

RPC and ledger evidence is bounded to ids, enum values, hashes, fingerprints, replay state, and next-action classes; raw provenance statement, signature, public key, Mode Pack payload, paths, prompts, provider responses, command output, and secrets are not returned or ledgered by route-resume metadata
non_goals: no generic workflow engine, scheduler, daemon, or background worker
no additional route families beyond selected-candidate fetch, provenance verification, and candidate approval
no active replacement, journey closure, automatic apply, recovery, verification retry, provider retry, parent join, shell, git, network, or service expansion
no report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or capability summary surface
rejected_alternatives: caller-side approval target construction as sufficient
generic route executor for all Mode Pack steps
mixing active replacement, completion closure, apply, or recovery into the same phase
technical_debt: M50.4 supports fetch, provenance, and approval route resume; active replacement, closure, uninterrupted Golden Journey, and crash/restart Golden Journey remain open.
The runtime monolith and large behavior-test module remain maintainability risks; module splitting should follow stable behavior slices rather than block Golden Journey capability.
M50 closeout should introduce finite Product DoD and deterministic stop evaluation so valuable phases continue only when they close an unfinished required DoD item.
Cross-version durable checkpoint recovery remains a later compatibility concern for long-running journeys that span runtime upgrades.
next_capability_rationale: After M50.4 merges, the next distinct M50 phase should derive active replacement from bounded approved-candidate evidence.
Do not add another wrapper around route state; keep moving route boundaries from caller-owned target assembly into Rust-owned replay-safe continuation.
